fields.meta_description: Build a field trip permission slip parents sign on a phone, with medical notes for chaperones and reminders for missing slips. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Field Trip Permission Slip Parents Sign on Their Phone
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent about the trip. It builds the field trip permission slip, collects each parent's signature and shows the teacher which families still have to sign.
fields.features_heading: What Every Permission Slip Has to Cover
fields.features_subheading: Trip days go wrong over one missing signature or an allergy nobody wrote down. Each part below closes that gap.
fields.feature_1:
Trip details above the signature

Put the destination and the return time at the top of the slip, with the cost and what to pack underneath. Parents read the whole day before they reach the line they sign.
fields.feature_2:
Signatures on a parent's phone

Take a drawn signature from a parent or guardian on whatever phone they carry. Each signed slip saves the signer's name and relationship to the student with a timestamp.
fields.feature_3:
Medical notes for the chaperones

Ask about allergies and medicines in separate fields, next to an emergency contact who can be reached during the trip. The trip nurse gets those answers grouped by bus.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders for missing slips

Email the families who have not signed yet, on the schedule you pick, with a link that opens their child's slip. Reminders stop for a family as soon as a parent signs it.
fields.feature_5:
A headcount drawn from the slips

Open a roster for each bus or group, made from the signed slips alone. A child without a signature shows in red, and the chaperone knows before anyone climbs aboard.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes with you

Export the full source of the slip and its database to your GitHub. A district developer can host it on school servers or connect it to the student system already in use.

fields.usecase_heading: Trips That Need a Signed Slip
fields.tab_content_1:
Two days out and four slips missing

Ms. Ortiz booked the aquarium for her Grade 3 class of 26 students. Two days before the trip, her dashboard shows 22 signed slips and 4 still out. Those families get an email with a link to their child's slip. Each new signature updates the count on her screen.
fields.tab_content_2:
The nurse sees every inhaler before the bus leaves

Westbrook High's band takes 2 buses to the state festival and stays overnight. The slip asks for an emergency contact and every medicine a student will carry. Each student signs a line under the parent's signature. The night before, the trip nurse gets the 5 students with medication, sorted by bus.
fields.tab_content_3:
Nine families read it in Spanish

Room 8 has 24 families, and 9 of them read Spanish first. Their slip opens in Spanish with the same questions and the same signature line. Both versions save to the same columns. Mr. Haddad sees all 24 slips in a single list, with a language column beside each name.
fields.tab_content_4:
The van roster comes from signed slips

Little Oaks Child Care takes the van to the public library on Thursday mornings. Before it leaves, the director opens a roster built from the signed slips: 11 children signed, 1 without a signature. That child stays at the center with a staff member, and the van leaves with 11.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Field Trip Permission Slip
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before the first field: knowing where the class is going, how it travels and who has to see the answers.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for medical and contact details
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the deadline and the reminders
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the destination, the date and the times the bus leaves and returns. Add the cost, what students should pack and whether lunch is provided. Parents decide from these lines, and they answer most of the questions teachers otherwise get by email.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for a phone number that will work on the day of the trip, then for allergies and any medicine the student will carry. Give each answer a field of its own. A chaperone on a bus needs a single answer fast, not a paragraph to read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the sentence a parent signs: their child may attend this trip, on this date, traveling this way. Name the school or center. For older students, add a declaration they sign themselves, as New York City's day trip form does for middle and high schoolers.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick a return date a few days before the trip. Decide when reminders go to families who have not signed and who watches the count. A deadline with no follow-up is how teachers end up phoning parents the night before a trip.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your trip details and the permission sentence into the prompt, and say who needs which answers. Emergent builds the slip and the database behind it. Change a question or move the deadline later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email the link to families or post it wherever they already get school notices. Every signature becomes a row in the database. The teacher's dashboard shows signed and missing slips for the class, and the nurse sees only the medical answers.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the slip on a phone as the parent of a made-up student, list a peanut allergy and sign. Check that the allergy reaches the chaperone's roster and that the count goes up. Have your principal or director read the wording before families see it.

Every one ends where the slip goes home in a backpack.
